name: Lambardar Ram Gopal
stand: Exposed drug peddlers in his village as a Nasha Virodhi Front activist.
standPa: ਨਸ਼ਾ ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਫਰੰਟ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਕੁਨ ਵਜੋਂ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਦੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ ਤਸਕਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਪਰਦਾਫਾਸ਼ ਕੀਤਾ।
story: Ram Gopal was the lambardar of Lakhanpal village and an activist with the Nasha Virodhi Front. Villagers and fellow activists said he spoke openly against the families selling drugs in the village and had exposed several peddlers. On a Saturday evening in January 2023 he was attacked and killed by a group of men while out on a walk with his brother-in-law. Six men from the village were booked for the murder, and residents blocked the Jandiala to Phagwara road the next morning demanding justice.

name: Harbhagwan Singh
stand: Joined his village's Nasha Roko Committee and asked a seller to stop.
standPa: ਪਿੰਡ ਦੀ ਨਸ਼ਾ ਰੋਕੋ ਕਮੇਟੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੋਏ ਅਤੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ ਵੇਚਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ।
story: Harbhagwan Singh worked as an outsourced lineman for the Punjab State Power Corporation and was the father of an 11-year-old daughter and an 8-year-old son. In August 2023 he joined the Nasha Roko Committee his village formed after children under 15 began falling into addiction. The committee reported a local seller to the police and, with the panchayat, asked him to stop. During a panchayat meeting, an alleged accomplice of the seller shot Harbhagwan dead. The seller and the shooter were later arrested.

name: Jasvir Singh
stand: Kept night watch on village roads to stop drug sellers.
standPa: ਨਸ਼ਾ ਵੇਚਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਪਿੰਡ ਦੇ ਰਾਹਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਠੀਕਰੀ ਪਹਿਰਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ।
story: Jasvir Singh was a member of his village's anti-drug action committee. On the night of 9 September 2023, committee volunteers were keeping thikri pehra, a traditional night watch, on the roads leading into Sidhana. When they tried to stop two men on a motorcycle, the men attacked Jasvir with a sharp weapon and killed him.
disputedNote: Police said their initial probe pointed to a personal dispute rather than a drug link.

name: Vikram Singh
stand: Opposed the drug peddlers in his village, villagers say.
standPa: ਪਿੰਡ ਵਾਸੀਆਂ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਦੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ ਤਸਕਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕੀਤਾ।
story: Residents of Killianwali say Vikram Singh was killed on 6 December 2024 after he opposed drug peddlers in the village. When the accused remained at large, villagers and farm union members blocked the Fazilka to Delhi national highway outside the DSP's office in Lambi. They lifted the blockade after police said the main accused had been arrested.

name: Sarpanch Mahinder Singh
stand: Passed information on chitta sellers to the police.
standPa: ਚਿੱਟਾ ਵੇਚਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਪੁਲਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ।
story: Mahinder Singh was the sarpanch of Buta Chhanna and a leader of the Jamhoori Kisan Sabha. Villagers said he regularly gave the police information about people selling chitta as part of the state's anti-drug campaign. On 28 February 2026, five men who had been waiting in the fields attacked him as he walked there with his wife. He suffered severe head injuries and died on 7 March. Three of the five accused were arrested, and villagers asked that a school be named after him.

name: ASI Sukhwinder Singh
stand: Stood in the path of suspected drug traffickers at a checkpoint.
standPa: ਨਾਕੇ 'ਤੇ ਸ਼ੱਕੀ ਨਸ਼ਾ ਤਸਕਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਰਾਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਖੜ੍ਹੇ ਹੋਏ।
story: Assistant Sub-Inspector Sukhwinder Singh of Punjab Police was posted at a checkpoint near Sardulgarh on the Barnala to Sirsa highway, set up to intercept suspected drug traffickers. When a car being chased by another police team approached, he stood in front of it to stop it. The driver ran him over and he died at the spot. Two men in the car were arrested.

name: Parvinder Singh
stand: Overcame addiction and confronted chemists selling intoxicating medicines.
standPa: ਨਸ਼ੇ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਨਸ਼ੀਲੀਆਂ ਦਵਾਈਆਂ ਵੇਚਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਕੈਮਿਸਟਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਮਣਾ ਕੀਤਾ।
story: Parvinder Singh, known to everyone as Jhota, had fought his own addiction and turned that experience into a campaign. He became one of the best known anti-drug voices in the Malwa region, using social media to confront chemists and peddlers selling intoxicating medicines, and his work inspired Nasha Roko Committees in villages across Mansa and Bathinda. On 13 October 2026 he went to a medical store in a busy Mansa market to question its owner about selling addictive medicine to an elderly man, recording the exchange live. The owner shot him. His death brought a statewide shutdown two days later. The CBI took over the investigation, and the Akal Takht declared him a martyr of the Sikh community.

name: Bikramjit Singh
stand: Objected, with two neighbours, to drugs sold in the village streets.
standPa: ਦੋ ਗੁਆਂਢੀਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲ ਕੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਦੀਆਂ ਗਲੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਕਦੇ ਨਸ਼ੇ ਦਾ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕੀਤਾ।
story: Villagers in Mari Pannuan say Bikramjit Singh and two others objected to drugs being sold openly in their streets on 15 October 2026, the day of the statewide shutdown over Parvinder Singh Jhota's killing. A large group attacked them with sharp weapons. Bikramjit died before he could reach medical care; Nishan Singh and Gurmukh Singh were injured. The Union Home Ministry sought a report from the state, and the Union Home Minister visited his family.
disputedNote: Police said the clash began over a mobile phone and ruled out a drug angle. Villagers and opposition leaders dispute this.
